decisions.reason: As a niche particle-therapy water phantom with weaker website prominence after launch and likely higher support and inventory costs, its option value appears more resolved and less attractive than the firm's core dosimetry lines.

A small-volume ionization chamber sits close to the firm's core capabilities and installed customer base, so with uncertain but plausible ongoing demand its option value still likely exceeds its carrying cost.
This product is another core dosimetry instrument for established clinical workflows, and absent clear negative evidence the firm would usually keep such a specialized option alive a bit longer.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models is tightly aligned with the firm's mainstream business and customer needs, making continued retention the most likely choice.
An ionization chamber for relative dosimetry complements the firm's QA portfolio and service model, so it is likely worth keeping unless stronger evidence of weak adoption emerges.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, synergistic product for radiation-therapy QA and likely has low enough ongoing carrying cost to justify staying on the market.
